title: finding(test-infra): `check-vi-mock-inherit` counts a spread that merely MENTIONS the obtained module as inheriting it
body:
Surfaced while sweeping `@object-ui/plugin-detail` for objectui#6892 slice 9 (PR pending on `claude/issue-6892-vi-mock-inherit-slice9-plugin-detail`). Filed unassigned, and **deliberately not repaired there** — that slice widens the covered set, it does not touch the recogniser.

## What was measured

`scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs` asks two things of a factory: does it OBTAIN the real module, and does the obtained value get SPREAD into the returned object. The second half is decided by `holdsObtainedModule()`, which tests whether the obtained token is **mentioned inside** a spread expression — not whether the module itself is the thing being spread.

So a spread of an object LITERAL that merely nests the obtained module passes, even though none of the module's exports reach the mock. Reproduced through the gate's own exported `findCallSites()` on `310c0ab19`, covered set restricted to one specifier:

| factory shape | gate verdict | correct verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: spread the obtained module directly | `inherits` | `inherits` |
| B: obtain, bind to a const, never spread | `frozen` | `frozen` |
| C: spread an object literal holding the obtained module | **`inherits`** | `frozen` |
| D: same as C, obtained bound to a const first | **`inherits`** | `frozen` |

C and D are false negatives. The gate reports the spread text as its reason, so the output even quotes the evasion back:

```
inherits  reason: ...({ _: await importOriginal() })
inherits  reason: ...({ _: actual })
```

In C and D the returned object carries exactly one inherited key — `_`, holding the module object — plus whatever the factory hand-lists. The next export any module in the file's import graph reads at module scope still resolves to `undefined`, which is the whole defect objectui#6849 built this gate to stop.

## Why this is an observation and not a live bug

Measured on the same tree, across all fourteen covered specifiers: **576 covered call sites judged `inherits`, of which 0 use the C/D shape.** Nothing in the repository evades the gate today, and neither shape is one a person writes by accident — both were constructed for a positive-control leg. So this is an unexercised hole in a guard, not a site currently passing that should not.

It is still worth closing, for the reason the gate's own header gives about `unreadable` and `indirect`: letting a shape through silently leaves the obvious way to evade the gate wide open, and this gate is green at rest, so an evasion has nothing to contrast against.

## Where the fix goes

`holdsObtainedModule()` in `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs`. The property it should test is that the spread's operand IS the obtained module — the obtained token as the whole expression, allowing `await`, parentheses and a member access chain — rather than the token appearing anywhere within the spread text. The pin `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts` already carries a negative-control block that C and D belong in.

⚠️ Re-derive before acting: the four rows above are one run of `findCallSites()` on `310c0ab19` against a single-specifier covered set, and objectui#7337 is the standing reminder that this recogniser has been wrong in both directions before.

Related: objectui#6892 (the per-specifier sweep worklist this came out of), objectui#7337 (the previous recogniser correction), objectui#7882 (the other open recogniser-adjacent card, on the shared comment masker).
